title: Algebraic Expressions and Simplification
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Algebraic Expressions and Simplification. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Reading an expression

An algebraic expression combines numbers, variables and operations without an equality sign. In (\(5x^2-3x+7\)), the terms are (\(5x^2\)), (\(-3x\)) and (\(7\)); their coefficients are 5, -3 and 7. The degree of a term is the sum of its variable exponents, so the first term has degree 2.

Collecting and operating

Like terms have exactly the same variables raised to the same powers. Add their coefficients: (\(4a-7a=-3a\)). Multiply every term when expanding: (\(m(n+p)=mn+mp\)). A negative sign before parentheses changes the sign of every term inside.

Identities and factorisation

Useful identities are (\(a+b\))^2=a^2+2ab+b^2, (a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2, and (\(a+b\))(a-b)=a^2-b^2. Factorisation reverses expansion by taking out a common factor or recognising an identity.

Worked example: Simplify (\(3(2x-1)-2(x+4)\)). Expanding gives (\(6x-3-2x-8=4x-11\)). At (\(x=3\)), the value is (\(12-11=1\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Write a subtraction as addition of the opposite before removing brackets.
  • Combine like terms only after expansion; (\(x\)) and (\(x^2\)) are unlike.
  • Check a factorisation by multiplying the factors back.
  • When evaluating, substitute a negative value in parentheses, such as (\((-2)^2\)).
  • Use a common factor first, then check for an identity.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Coefficient is the signed numerical factor; constant term has no variable.
  • (\(x+x=2x\)), whereas (\(x \times x=x^2\)).
  • (\(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\)).
  • For a polynomial, degree is the largest exponent after like terms are combined.
  • Equivalent expressions have the same value for every permitted variable value.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Simplify (\(4(2x+3)-3x\)).

    1. (\(5x+12\))
    2. (\(8x+9\))
    3. (\(5x+3\))
    4. (\(11x+12\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(5x+12\))

    Distribute 4: (\(8x+12-3x=5x+12\)).

  2. Core:

    Evaluate (\(a^2-2ab+b^2\)) for (\(a=5,b=2\)).

    1. (\(5\))
    2. (\(9\))
    3. (\(13\))
    4. (\(25\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(9\))

    Substitute: (\(25-20+4=9\)). Equivalently, the expression is (\((a-b)^2=3^2=9\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Simplify (\(5a-3b+2a+8b\)).

    1. (\(7a+5b\))
    2. (\(7a-11b\))
    3. (\(3a+5b\))
    4. (\(7ab\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(7a+5b\))

    Collect like terms: (\(5a+2a=7a\)) and (\(-3b+8b=5b\)). The result is (\(7a+5b\)).

  4. Standard:

    Expand and simplify (\(2(3x-4)-3(x+1)\)).

    1. (\(3x-11\))
    2. (\(9x-5\))
    3. (\(3x-5\))
    4. (\(9x-11\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3x-11\))

    Distribute: (\(6x-8-3x-3=3x-11\)).

  5. Challenge:

    If (\(p+q=9\)) and (\(pq=14\)), evaluate (\(p^2+q^2\)).

    1. (\(25\))
    2. (\(53\))
    3. (\(67\))
    4. (\(81\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(53\))

    Use (\((p+q)^2=p^2+2pq+q^2\)). Thus (\(p^2+q^2=9^2-2(14)=81-28=53\)).
